model.title: Common Cents Act
model.meta: Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee · Sen. Cynthia Lummis (R-WY)

summary.text: The bill would stop the U.S. Treasury from making new pennies for everyday use, except as needed for collectors, while keeping the penny legal tender. It would require cash payments and transfers to be rounded to a multiple of five cents, applying to sellers, other cash transfers, and cash wages paid to employees. It would also let the Treasury stop minting any coin for circulation if it follows required steps, including notice and a briefing to Congress. The Federal Reserve Board would periodically report on a plan for accepting penny orders and deposits at commercial coin terminals. Finally, it would allow the nickel to be made from a different material, such as a zinc core with an outer layer of nickel, in addition to the current copper-nickel alloy.
